messages.content: "Can you help me plan a trip? I need to know the distance in kilometers from New York to London using the 'geodistance.find' function, then I want to know the time difference between New York and London using the 'timezones.get_difference' function. After that, I want to find flights from New York to London on the date of 'next friday' using the 'flights.search' function. Finally, I want to know the distance in miles from London to Paris using the 'geodistance.find' function again."

function.name: flights_search
function.description: Find flights between two cities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

date.description: The date to fly. Default is today if not specified.

function.name: timezones_get_difference
function.description: Find the time difference between two cities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: geodistance_find
function.description: Find the distance between two cities on the globe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

origin.description: The originating city for the distance calculation.

destination.description: The destination city for the distance calculation.

unit.description: The unit of measure for the distance calculation.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to call multiple functions sequentially. We need to use the function calls. The user wants:

1. Distance in kilometers from New York to London using geodistance.find. So we call geodistance_find with origin="New York", destination="London", unit="kilometers".

2. Time difference between New York and London using timezones_get_difference. So call timezones_get_difference with city1="New York", city2="London".

3. Flights from New York to London on date "next friday". So call flights_search with from_city="New York", to_city="London", date="next friday".

4. Distance in miles from London to Paris using geodistance_find again. So call geodistance_find with origin="London", destination="Paris", unit="miles".

We need to output the function calls in JSON format. According to guidelines, we should output each function call as separate JSON objects. But the instructions say: "When calling a function, respond with a JSON object containing the name of the function and arguments. Do not add any additional keys or text." And "If you need to call multiple functions, you can do so in a single response, but you must separate them into distinct JSON objects." So we need to produce multiple JSON objects separated by newlines. That is allowed.

Thus we will produce four JSON objects, each on its own line. No other text. Let's do that.
